tagline: Luxury residential homebuilder and master-planned community developer
hero_kpi_rationale: Backlog is the primary leading indicator of future revenues in the homebuilding sector, reflecting committed demand and short-term visibility on expected deliveries.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of homes sold but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog stands at 4,647 homes valued at $5.49 billion as of October 31, 2025, compared to $6.47 billion one year earlier.
kpis.signal: Backlog declining despite sustained structural residential demand.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from home and land sales.
kpis.description: Revenue reached $10.97 billion in 2025, a slight increase from $10.85 billion in 2024.
kpis.signal: Modest revenue growth despite a tight market.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income decreased from $1.57 billion in 2024 to $1.35 billion in 2025, partly due to non-recurring items in the prior year.
kpis.signal: Decline in net income despite revenue stability.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: Calculated from $10.97 billion in revenue and implied cost of sales, gross margin is approximately 24.6% in 2025, down from 25.1% in 2024.
kpis.signal: High gross margin for the homebuilding sector but slight contraction.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin is estimated at approximately 14.8% in 2025, down from 16.9% in 2024, linked to cost pressures and demand softness.

kpis.name: Net Contract Value
kpis.explanation: Total value of new contracts after cancellations.
kpis.description: Net contract value signed in 2025 amounts to $9.85 billion for 9,943 homes, down 2.2% from $10.07 billion in 2024.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in new orders reflecting affordability pressures.

kpis.name: Home Sites Controlled
kpis.explanation: Number of lots available for construction.
kpis.description: Home sites controlled reached 76,100 as of October 31, 2025, up from 74,700 one year earlier, including 33,000 owned lots and 43,100 controlled through options.
kpis.signal: Growth in land portfolio despite lot consumption.

kpis.name: Spec Homes
kpis.explanation: Proportion of homes built without a prior buyer in the sales strategy.
kpis.description: The company has strategically increased the number of spec homes to meet demand for shorter delivery timelines. This strategy helps address volatile market conditions and weak demand.
kpis.signal: Strategic increase in spec homes to reduce delivery timelines.

risks.title: Technology failures and data security breaches
risks.score_rationale: The company explicitly mentions risks related to information technology failures and data security breaches, which could harm operational activities and customer trust.

risks.title: Intense competition in the sector
risks.score_rationale: The homebuilding sector is highly competitive and fragmented, with numerous builders of varying sizes, which could affect the company's sales and margins.

risks.title: Regulatory risks and government approvals
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to numerous regulations and government approvals. Obtaining permits and approvals may result in significant delays and additional costs in community development.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risks
risks.score_rationale: The company explicitly mentions cybersecurity risks with dedicated governance (Audit and Risk Committee, CIO, CISO). Cybersecurity incidents could have a significant impact on operations, customer data, and reputation.

risks.title: Economic risks and market slowdown
risks.score_rationale: The company experienced weak demand in 2025 attributed to affordability pressures and volatile economic conditions affecting consumer confidence. These macroeconomic factors could persist and negatively impact sales volumes.

ai_positioning.summary: Toll Brothers does not mention any artificial intelligence strategy or initiative in its recent financial filings. The focus remains on construction, land development, and traditional real estate services, including smart home technology.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning technologies in the 10-K
